Aurora borealis weaves through the ribcage of a fallen wyrm, emerald and violet curtains rippling where wings once beat, as if the northern lights mourn the ancient beast's passing.
Twin moons rise simultaneously behind the dragon's skull, one amber and one silver, their reflected light pooling in the creature's empty eye sockets like ghostly luminescence from forgotten days.
Blood moon hangs low over the skeletal remains, bathing bleached bones in crimson light, transforming the peaceful ruin into a scene of fresh carnage as shadows deepen between vertebrae.

Lightning storm illuminates the collapsed dragon-temple in stroboscopic flashes, each bolt revealing new angles of devastation—shattered columns, scattered scales, the terrible beauty of ruin frozen in electric blue.
Solar eclipse darkens the sky as the party reaches the hoard, corona blazing around the black sun like a dragon's final breath, casting the treasure in otherworldly twilight.
Meteor shower streaks overhead, each burning trail reflected in the dragon's scattered hoard-coins, as if the heavens themselves rain fire in tribute to the fallen guardian below.
Distant living dragon soars across the horizon, its silhouette momentarily visible against storm clouds, the only remaining witness to its fallen kin's ancient majesty and subsequent desolation.
God-rays pierce the broken cathedral dome, illuminating dust motes and a single massive dragon skull in shafts of golden light, transforming bones into something almost holy.
Heavy snowfall blankets the dragon skeleton, softening harsh angles with white silence, each rib becoming a gentle hill, winter claiming what fire and time could not erase.
Fog rolls through the ruined colonnade where the dragon fell, tendrilous and thick, obscuring and revealing bone-segments in waves, making the enormous corpse seem to breathe again.
Petrified dragonfire still flickers mid-air above the scattered hoard, blue-white flames frozen in time yet somehow dancing, cold as starlight, casting no heat but endless eerie illumination.
Will-o-wisps cluster inside the massive dragon skull, pale green lights drifting through eye sockets and between teeth, drawn to the lingering essence of ancient magic and memory.
Ghostly dragon-shape materializes briefly in the evening mist, translucent wings spreading over the physical remains below, before dissolving like breath on winter air—echo without substance.
Beacon-fires ignite on distant mountain ridges in succession, their smoke columns rising against twilight, answering some ancient signal the dragon's presence once commanded from the living world.
Distant pyre-smoke rises black against the sunset, marking another dragon's funeral far across the plains, the sky itself becoming monument to a dying age of scaled majesty.
Rune-stones surrounding the fallen dragon pulse with faint blue luminescence as night falls, ancient wards still functioning though their charge has long since perished, duty outlasting life.
Ground-fog blankets the chamber floor with phosphorescent shimmer, transforming the hoard into an island of gold floating on glowing mist, unreachable and dreamlike in its beauty.
Storm-front advances with massive crepuscular rays piercing through, light-columns striking down around the dragon skeleton like celestial spears, nature's tribute to the fallen titan beneath.
Dust-motes swirl through shafts of evening light penetrating the ruined vault, each particle catching gold and amber, the air itself seeming to mourn in slow-dancing constellations.
White petals drift through the colonnade where the dragon lies, carried by spring wind through broken arches, settling on bones like snow, nature's gentle reclamation of death.
Comet blazes across the night sky directly above the ruins, its tail spreading wide as dragon wings, ancient omen marking the hour when wyrm-bones gleam under celestial fire.
Winter sunrise strikes through the cathedral's shattered rose window, projecting colored light across the dragon's skull in fragments—ruby, sapphire, emerald—a crown for the fallen king.
Harvest moon rises enormous and orange behind the skeletal wings, so close and large it seems the dragon might have grasped it in life, treasure beyond all gold.
Sheet lightning flickers continuously within distant storm clouds, silent and purple, backlighting the dragon skeleton in perpetual twilight, as if the sky itself holds vigil over ancient bones.
Morning mist parts suddenly as wind shifts, revealing the full scale of the skeleton in one breathtaking moment before fog closes again, wonder glimpsed and lost like memory.
